draft.title: Temperature and internal energy
card: All the particles in a substance are moving and pulling on each other. Internal energy is the total of their kinetic energy and their potential energy.
Temperature is linked to the average kinetic energy of the particles. Hotter means the particles move faster on average.
Adding energy to a substance raises its internal energy. The particles can gain kinetic energy, potential energy, or both.
The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, where particles have the least possible energy. Absolute zero is about 273 degrees below 0 on the Celsius scale, so T(K) = T(°C) + 273.
draft.remember: Internal energy is the particles' kinetic plus potential energy. Temperature tracks the average kinetic energy.

a.q: Which statement best describes the internal energy of a block of copper?
opts: The sum of kinetic and potential energy of its particles
The kinetic energy of the whole block as it moves
The average speed of the particles in the block
The potential energy of the block above the ground
a.why: Internal energy is the total of the kinetic and potential energy of the particles inside the substance. The average speed or kinetic energy of the particles relates to temperature, not to the total, and the motion or height of the whole block does not change it.
a.clue: Think about the particles inside, not the block as a whole.

b.q: A lab thermometer reads 27 °C. What is this temperature on the Kelvin scale?
b.why: Add 273 to the Celsius value: 27 + 273 = 300 K. Subtracting 273 gives 246, which reverses the conversion. Kelvin has no negative values, as it starts at absolute zero.
b.clue: Kelvin values are always larger than Celsius values.

a.best: The sum of kinetic and potential energy of its particles

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'Subtracting 273 gives 246'. In fact 27 − 273 = −246, which is the −246 K option. 246 comes from 273 − 27. The explanation miscalculates and confuses the two wrong options.
